slides.1.title: The Science of Old Vines: Why Do They Make Better Wine?
slides.1.html:
"Old vines" (Old Vines / Vieilles Vignes / Velhas Vinhas) is not a legally defined term, but the industry widely believes that old vines bring higher quality.

🔬 Old Vines vs. Young Vines

  • Deep root systems: the roots of vines aged 30+ years can reach 15–30 metres deep (especially in schist and granite), drawing on deep groundwater and minerals
  • Naturally low yields: old vines reduce yields by themselves, so each vine carries very little fruit, but with markedly greater concentration and complexity
  • Root memory: deep roots make the vine less affected by surface climate, so vintage variation is more stable
  • Richer minerals: deep minerals are absorbed through the roots and show in the wine's minerality

📅 Classification of Old Vines in Portugal (unofficial)

  • Old vines (Vinha Velha): 30–60 years, naturally low yields, improved quality
  • Very old vines: 60–100 years, rare, with greatly increased fruit complexity
  • Century-old vines (Centenária): 100+ years, extremely rare, representing the finest wine grapes
  • Ungrafted old vines (Ramisco de Colares): own-rooted old vines, some over a century old, the rarest in the world
slides.2.title: Portugal's Most Important Old-Vine Regions
slides.2.items.0.label: Colares (sand-dune old vines)
slides.2.items.0.desc: Own-rooted (ungrafted) old Ramisco vines, some over a century old, protected by sand dunes with roots reaching deep into the sand. The rarest in the world, with annual output possibly no more than a few thousand bottles
slides.2.items.1.label: Douro old vines (schist terraces)
slides.2.items.1.desc: Century-old Touriga Nacional・Touriga Franca, with roots 20 metres deep in schist and concentrated minerality. The old-vine bottlings of Barca Velha・Quinta do Crasto are the finest Douro reds
slides.2.items.2.label: Vinho Verde old-vine Alvarinho
slides.2.items.2.desc: 50–80-year-old vines on the granite of Monção/Melgaço, with deeper minerality and more complex acidity. Very low yields but outstanding quality
slides.2.items.3.label: Bairrada old-vine Baga
slides.2.items.3.desc: 50–100-year-old Baga vines on Bairrada clay-limestone, a concentrated version of high acidity and tannin that needs 20+ years of ageing, and one of the world's most underrated old-vine reds
slides.3.question: Why have Colares' old Ramisco vines been able to remain own-rooted (ungrafted) and survive for over a century, making it a rare ungrafted old-vine region?
slides.3.options.0: Because Colares' climate is especially cold and the vines grow slowly
slides.3.options.2: Because the vines are planted in Atlantic coastal sand dunes, where phylloxera cannot survive in sandy soil, and they were never affected by the 19th-century phylloxera epidemic
slides.3.options.3: Because special genetically modified varieties were used
slides.3.explanation: The key to Colares' Ramisco old vines surviving for centuries is the sand-dune soil: phylloxera cannot survive in loose sand, so the phylloxera disaster that destroyed the European wine industry in the 19th century did not affect Colares. The vines did not need to be grafted onto phylloxera-resistant rootstocks and kept their original roots, with some vines having survived 200–300 years or more.
slides.4.question: What is the main quality advantage of old vines (30+ years) over young vines?
slides.4.options.0: Old vines can produce more fruit
slides.4.options.1: Old-vine wines can be drunk immediately, with no ageing needed
slides.4.options.2: Old vines have deeper roots and naturally low yields, giving fruit of greater concentration and complexity and drawing up more deep minerals
slides.4.explanation: The key advantages of old vines are: ① deep roots (up to 15–30 metres) draw up deep minerals; ② naturally low yields (old vines reduce crop by themselves), so each bunch concentrates more of the essence; ③ deep roots make the vine less affected by climate, with less vintage variation. Together these give old-vine wines greater concentration, complexity and minerality.
